title: ticfac leaves its temp dirs behind: 1,370 ticfac-* dirs in TMPDIR, growing without bound
description: Found 2026-09-27: $TMPDIR (/var/folders/.../T) holds ~1,370 ticfac-* dirs, 11 GB, dating back to Sep 12: ticfac-tracker (603), ticfac-gate (240), ticfac-merge (225), ticfac-reconcile-bin (93), ticfac-index (78), ticfac-gate-io (73), ticfac-tracker-index (34), plus cli-registry, exec-bin, door-harness. Some come from runs (tracker/merge/gate trees made with os.MkdirTemp and git worktree add, not removed on every path, including SIGTERM), some from tests that don't use t.TempDir. About 10 are still registered as git worktrees of the main checkout. Find each creator, remove on every exit path (defer, the evacuation path, t.TempDir in tests), and have ticfac doctor (or run start) sweep ticfac-* dirs whose owning pid is gone.
acceptance_criteria: A full reconcile test run and a run-epic start/stop cycle leave no new ticfac-* dirs in TMPDIR; a test asserts it for the tracker/merge/gate temp trees
closed_reason: Fixed by internal/tempdir. Each temp dir is named ticfac-<kind>-p<pid>-* and its cleanup is registered, and a worktree is removed with worktree remove --force before its dir. run-epic's signal handler runs tempdir.ReleaseAll before os.Exit, which leaked every open tree before. A returning run releases whatever it abandoned. At start, run-epic sweeps ticfac-* dirs in os.TempDir() whose pid is dead and whose contents are untouched for 24h, skipping gate-slots roots; Run's worktree prune drops their registrations. The reconcile and exec/subprocess TestMains keep TMPDIR inside their pid-named bin dir, so a killed suite leaves 1 sweepable dir instead of ~28. Tests: TestARunLeavesNoTempTreesBehind, TestTempTreesGoOnEveryPathIncludingTheSignalExit, the SIGTERM evacuation test (child leaves no ticfac-* dirs), and the tempdir Sweep tests.
